title: The 4Ps of Marketing Explained Simply | Marketing Management Ep 13
description:
Zoya found her customer, busy parents, and made them a big jar of eighteen laddoos for Rs 360, sold only from Nani's kitchen. It flopped. The customer was right, but the mix was wrong. In this animated lesson, the Laddoo Lab team plans again and builds the marketing mix, the 4Ps: product, price, place and promotion.

You will see Kotler and Armstrong's definition of the marketing mix, how Neil Borden made the phrase famous in 1953 with twelve ingredients, and how E. Jerome McCarthy grouped them into four Ps in 1960. Then we run Mrs. Rao's week twice, through four gates in the order a customer meets them: the old jar fails at every gate, while the new six-pack (Rs 120 for six, delivered every Monday, promoted with posters and free tastes) opens all four. We see the 4Ps at work today in a phone maker, a cinema, a bakery and a hospital, and look honestly at the limits: the 4Ps are simple, but they look from the seller's side, which is why Robert Lauterborn proposed the 4Cs in 1990.

This is Episode 13 of our Marketing Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
